record.tranche_reason: This perspective article argues that alignment may make models easier to subvert, but it does not test the refusal-direction claim or any listed version. Its examples and cited findings do not test whether that direction mediates refusal.
record.gate_note: The article cites other works for model steering and jailbreak findings; those are not this study's results. It gives one illustrative ChatGPT refusal example in the output-tinkering discussion, recorded as an unversioned finding because it does not test any listed mechanism or intervention.
record.test_reason: Perspective article with no experiments. It cites the refusal-direction paper [1] only as general support that internal-state geometry captures behavioural dichotomies. Its steering and jailbreak points are attributed to cited works. The single ChatGPT refusal example is anecdotal and involves no direction intervention, so no version is tested.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct in substance. The authors argue that better alignment may make models easier to misalign through model, input or output tinkering (the 'AI alignment paradox'). They call for formal study and mitigation of the paradox.
record.recipe_differences: No measurement or intervention recipe is tested.

fits_no_version.finding: The article reports that ChatGPT refused one request to rewrite text so it justifies Putin's attack, but complied with the reverse rewrite.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Aligned chat models refuse value-inverting rewrites but comply with value-aligning rewrites, enabling the collection of paired data for value editors.

record.problems: The article is a perspective piece and provides no controlled experiment or systematic measurements on the refusal-direction claim. Its ChatGPT example is anecdotal.
record.rows_left_out: No further rows: the article's other model-tinkering, jailbreak, and value-editor examples are conceptual or attributed to cited work rather than reported as this study's own test results.

untested.parts: All: difference-in-means direction, ablation, addition, preservation of other abilities.
All. Jailbreaks are discussed conceptually via cited work [10], with no direction measurement.
All. The 'stronger alignment yields a more separable direction' idea is argued conceptually, not tested.

record.verdict_notes: Relation changed from 'discusses' to 'cites_only'. The article cites Arditi et al. [1] in passing and does not engage with the direction claim. Stated venue (Communications of the ACM) is not given in the text. The reader's statement that it was peer reviewed there is unverified.

rows.subject: ChatGPT

conditions.value: Request to recast the text in justification of the attack

rows.measure: Whether the model refuses the requested rewrite
rows.value: The article says ChatGPT refuses the request.
